claims.head: The Golden Knights are likely to tilt the ice
claims.body: The Golden Knights have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Sharks one of the worst. Expect the Golden Knights to spend more of the night in the Sharks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

notes.text: Noah Hanifin is on injured reserve and has missed the last 7 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Parker Wotherspoon has taken his spot beside Dylan Coghlan. That pair has had 69% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 75:33 together, up from 43% with Hanifin.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 16 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Ivar Stenberg has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 61% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 68:04 together, about what it had with Chernyshov (60%).
Kiefer Sherwood is on injured reserve and has missed the last 4 games.
Jacob Trouba is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Nolan Allan has taken his spot beside Sam Dickinson.

stakes: The Sharks go in tied for fourth in the Pacific with 24 points, 11 points behind the Golden Knights, second.

SJS.head: Not an easy night for the Sharks
SJS.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage and Vegas will be without Hanifin, the Golden Knights have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks’ best way through is keeping shots to a minimum.

VGK.head: The matchup suits the Golden Knights
VGK.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage and Vegas will be without Hanifin, the Golden Knights have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Stone’s favorite opponent
paras: The Sharks (11-14-2) lost 7-0 to Anaheim on Wednesday, while the Golden Knights have won two in a row. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Knights second (tied for fourth in the NHL) and the Sharks fifth (tied for 21st). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
This season, the Golden Knights have outscored teams 88-75, but only 55-53 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 26-16.

The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st), have one of the league’s best penalty kills (2nd) and create chances on the penalty kill (2nd). On the other side, the Sharks ice the puck a lot (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (32nd). They also have a leaky penalty kill (31st), so the Golden Knights’ power play (4th) could do real damage when they’re shorthanded. San Jose has scored 2.52 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 3.67, the fourth most. Good looks are likely to be hard to come by for the Sharks.

Jack Eichel (11 G / 22 A / 33 P in 26 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games and a point in nine straight games against San Jose. Mitch Marner (4 G / 25 A / 29 P in 24 GP) is next in line. The Sharks’ scoring runs through Macklin Celebrini (10 G / 21 A / 31 P in 25 GP), who has seven points in his last five games.
Carter Hart (8-4-2 / .885 SV% in 14 GS) is expected to start for Vegas, and Yaroslav Askarov (6-10-1 / .889 SV% in 17 GS) for San Jose.
The Golden Knights usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.
